Under the market approach, management utilized the guideline public company method, which analyzes market multiples (including revenue and/or earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization) for a group of comparable public companies, and used this market approach to validate the results of the income approach. intro.text: LKQ Corporation ("LKQ," the "Company" or "we") is a global distributor of vehicle products, including replacement parts, components and systems used in the repair and maintenance of vehicles, and specialty aftermarket products and accessories to improve the performance, functionality and appearance of vehicles. Buyers of vehicle replacement products have the option to purchase from primarily four sources: new products produced by original equipment manufacturers ("OEMs"); new products produced by companies other than the OEMs, which are referred to as aftermarket products; salvaged products taken from total loss vehicles; and reconditioned products that have been refurbished or remanufactured. Collectively, we refer to the three sources that are not new OEM products as alternative parts.

lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: During the year ended December 31, 2025, parts and services revenue represented 97.5% of our consolidated revenue.
Our operations outside of the U.S. represented 54.4% of our revenue during both years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024.

In 2025, approximately 44% of our aftermarket purchases were made from our top six vendors, with our largest vendor accounting for approximately 13% of our annual inventory purchases for the North America segment.
This concentration is largely attributable to our paint, body and equipment ("PBE") business, through which we established a strategic relationship with a key supplier of paint and related products.

Approximately 49% of our aftermarket products in 2025 were purchased from vendors located in the U.S.; however, we believe that most of these products were manufactured in Taiwan, Mexico, or other foreign countries.
These customers represent the primary source of revenue for the segment.
In 2025, our largest supplier accounted for 7% of aftermarket inventory purchases within our Europe segment, and no other supplier represented more than 5% of purchases.
During the year, 93% of our products were sourced from companies located in Europe, and 74% and 17% of our total inventory purchases were denominated in euros and pounds sterling, respectively.

In 2025, approximately 19% of our specialty vehicle aftermarket purchases were made from our top three suppliers, with our largest supplier accounting for approximately 10% of our annual inventory purchases.
Our customers are principally small, independent businesses that rely on us to provide a broad range of products, rapid delivery, marketing support and technical assistance.

We believe that a majority of collision parts by dollar amount are supplied by the OEMs, with the balance being supplied by distributors of alternative aftermarket, recycled, refurbished and remanufactured collision parts like us.
We rely upon insurance companies and our customers to promote the usage of alternative parts.

We rely on business relationships with insurance companies and our customers, and our success depends, in part, on the acceptance and promotion of alternative parts usage by automotive insurance companies and vehicle repair facilities.

We rely on these relationships for sales to some repair shops, and a modification or termination of these relationships may result in a loss of sales, which could adversely affect our results of operations.

Our business depends on vehicle accidents, mechanical failures and routine maintenance for both the demand for repairs using our products and services and the supply of recycled, remanufactured and refurbished parts.

Our Specialty segment depends on sales of pickup trucks, sport utility vehicles, crossover utility vehicles, high performance vehicles, marine vehicles and RVs; any reduction in the number of such vehicles in operation will adversely affect demand for our Specialty products.
We rely on third parties to provide products, services and data relating to our industry that are integral to our operations.

The extent to which other public health emergencies could impact our business, results of operations, financial condition or liquidity is highly uncertain and would depend on future developments, including the spread and duration of any such virus and the variants thereof, potential actions taken by governmental authorities and how quickly economic conditions stabilize and recover.

Our ability to make scheduled payments on or to refinance our debt obligations depends on our financial condition and operating performance, which are subject to prevailing economic and competitive conditions and to certain financial, business and other factors beyond our control.

We rely on information technology and communication systems in critical areas of our operations and a disruption relating to such technology and systems, including cybersecurity threats, could harm our business.

In the ordinary course of business, we rely upon IT networks and systems, some of which are provided by or leased from third parties, to process, transmit and store electronic information and to manage and support a variety of business processes and activities.

Whether the process will result in any transaction, our ability to complete any such transaction, and if the Board decides to pursue one or more transactions, will depend on numerous factors, some of which are beyond our control.

See the risk factor titled “ We rely on information technology and communication systems in critical areas of our operations and a disruption relating to such technology and systems, including cybersecurity threats, could harm our business. ” in Part I, Item 1A of this Annual Report on Form 10-K for further information.

The payment of any future dividends will be at the discretion of our Board and will depend upon our results of operations, financial condition, business prospects, capital requirements, contractual restrictions, any potential indebtedness we may incur, restrictions imposed by applicable law, tax considerations and other factors that our Board deems relevant.
Our primary sources of liquidity are cash flows from operations and our revolving credit facilities.
Our future liquidity and capital requirements will depend upon numerous factors, including the costs and timing of our internal development efforts and the success of those efforts.

(1) Guarantor subsidiaries recorded $51 million and $53 million of net sales to and $259 million and $286 million of purchases from non-guarantor subsidiaries for the fiscal years ended December 31, 2025 and December 31, 2024, respectively.
An aftermarket product is a new vehicle product manufactured by a company other than the original equipment manufacturer.

s.t: As of September 30, 2026, the Level 1 fair value of our investment in Mekonomen was $ 103 million based on the quoted market price for Mekonomen's common stock using the same foreign exchange rate as the carrying value.
During the nine months ended September 30, 2026 , we recorded a $44 million other-than-temporary impairment related to our equity method investment in Mekonomen.

During the three months ended September 30, 2026, the share price of Mekonomen fell below our carrying value and we evaluated this investment for other-than-temporary impairment, determining that the decline in fair value was not other-than-temporary.
Therefore, we recognized an other-than-temporary impairment charge of $ 44 million, which represented the difference in the carrying value and the fair value of our investment in Mekonomen.
The fair value of our investment in Mekonomen was determined using the Mekonomen share price of SEK 69 as of March 31, 2026.
